messages:
alice: Heads-up: I'm sketching a fallback policy for when an org-level API key exceeds quota. Question: should we route to the project's SA key automatically, or surface an explicit opt-in in the console?
ben: my gut is automatic routing for short bursts (like 5m) then surface in console if it persists. keeps user apps alive.
carol: automatic makes sense but we need signal clarity in logs/metrics. ops should be able to tell "we routed because org key throttled".
dom: agree on logs. also need to think about billing attribution — org vs project. If we route, which billing bucket gets charged?
alice: good call. proposal: charge original org until routing lasts >10m, then switch attribution to project. that matches expected intent.
samir: that could be surprising. what if project doesn't belong to same billing owner? need guardrails and an admin override.
lisa: from a UX standpoint, adding an explicit per-org toggle in console for "allow fallback to project SAs" would be ideal. default on but admins can opt out.
carol: ok but default-on + audit logs + email alert for admins when fallback occurs. also add a small banner in Console's Deployments view: "Traffic routed to project SA due to org key quota".
ben: telemetry: add a new metric: auth.fallback.count and auth.fallback.latency_penalty. Also tag with fallback.reason and fallback.target (project_id/service_account).
alice: can we also attach the original request trace id so traces link across? would help chasing perf regressions.
dom: technically doable via trace propagation header. need to make sure we scrub any PII.
samir: security question: if fallback uses project SA, do we impersonate or mint a short-lived token? Prefer minting ephemeral token with scoped permissions rather than reusing SA long-term creds.
carol: yep ephemeral tokens + minted claims that preserve original org/project provenance. store a mapping in audit log.
alice: and what about rate-limit semantics? If we route to a project SA that has lower quota, should we enforce the original org limits first?
ben: implement a hierarchical limiter: evaluate request against org quota then projected target quota. if target can't handle it, try alternate fallback (another regional project) or queue with 429.
lisa: UX flow: when fallback happens, Console notification should link to a small modal explaining why and who to contact (owner). also provide a one-click revoke fallback permission for admins.
carol: rollout plan: feature flag behind org-level toggle, start with internal orgs, include a dry-run where we simulate routing and surface telemetry only.
alice: testing: we need unit tests for routing decision tree + e2e canary hitting quota with traffic replay. schedule a 2-week canary.
dom: ops playbook: if fallback causes billing surprise, runbook to revert with a single switch and notify all owners.
samir: one more: add a guard where fallback is refused if project SA doesn't have required scopes for the route. otherwise we could silently break behavior.
ben: good. auth-bot: deploy plan note: create feature flag, add telemetry fields, add console toggle, add audit events.
auth-bot: [deploy-bot] Feature flag created: ff/auth-fallback (staging=true).
